main_text.p: egregiè inferuiunt. Nam si spectes, 1. caufsa efficientem, principem, videlicet Deum, quum is pater nofter sit, & iustissimè, moderatissimè & benignissimè nobiscū semper agat, non est cur despondeamus sub eius ferula animos. Iuxta dictum: Obmutui non aperui os meum: quia tu istud fecisti. Psal. 39. 10.
2. Materiam, seu subiectum, Quem diligit Deus, castigat: & flagellat quemcunq; filium recipit. Heb. 12. 6.

3. Formam, Deus nos castigando erudit. Iuxta illud: Bonū est mihi Domine, quòd humiliasti me, vt discerem iustificationes tuas. Item, Antequam humiliarer, errabam. Enimuerò in crucis Schola ea discimus, quæ nunquam aliàs assequi possemus.
4. Finem, Deus nos castigat, tum vt in nobis caro mortificetur, tum ne cum hoc mundo pereamus. 1. Cor. 11. 32.
main_text.head: DE THESI ANTEISAGOGE.
main_text.p: Bibent omnes gentes iugiter. Hoc hemistichium, sic exposuit Ieremias propheta cap. 25. vt Solem admotis facibus iuuare velle, videri possit, quisque aliquid ei illustrando addere conetur. Itaque Thesim subiungam.

page.notes: Printed text is in a smaller, mixed type; the heading "DE THESI ANTEISAGOGE" is written in spaced capitals with Greek letters (ΑΝΤΕΙΣΑΓΩΓΗ) in the original; I transcribed the Greek word as Latin letters only where the Greek was not legible with confidence. The last line is cut off at the foot and continues "dicem" on the next line as printed. Marginal numerals 2, 3, 4 are the side notes beside the first paragraphs. Words such as "Antequam" and "humiliarer" are as printed. Greek in the heading and the catchword line: illegible in this scan at the resolution provided. Uncertain readings are not marked; please verify the heading against the scan.
